stem.text: The number of deer P in a forest is modeled by the differential equation \( \frac{dP}{dt} = \frac{2 P}{5} - \frac{P^{2}}{1250} \), where t is measured in years, and \( P(0) = 200 \). Without solving the equation, find the limit of P as t increases without bound, and the value of P at which P is growing fastest.

answer_key.label: P approaches \( 500 \) deer as t increases without bound, and P is growing fastest when \( P = 250 \) deer.

worked_solution.text: The right side equals \( \frac{2}{5}P\left(1 - \frac{P}{500}\right) \), which is 0 at P = 0 and at P = 500, so the carrying capacity is 500.
worked_solution.rule_named: zeros of the logistic right side

worked_solution.text: For 0 < P < 500 the right side is positive, and P(0) = 200 lies in that range, so P increases and approaches 500 deer as t increases without bound.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the rate gives the limit

worked_solution.text: The right side is a quadratic in P that opens downward with zeros at 0 and 500, so it is largest halfway between them, at P = 250 deer; P passes through that value because it starts below it.

options.label: P approaches \( 200 \) deer as t increases without bound, and P is growing fastest when \( P = 250 \) deer.
options.derivation: a limit named without using the sign of the rate, the initial value taken as the level the population settles at

options.derivation: the limiting value read from the other zero of the right side, P = 0
